text: A song of ascents. Of David. I rejoiced when they said to me, "Let us go to the house of the LORD."
Our feet are standing in your gates, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, built as a city bound firmly together,
where the tribes go up, the tribes of the LORD, as a decree for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the LORD.

versions.text: where the tribes go up, the tribes of the LORD, as a testimony for Israel, to praise the name of the LORD.
versions.explanation: עֵדוּת here functions as an ordinance or decree binding on Israel (the pilgrimage requirement), and לְהֹדוֹת is specifically 'to give thanks,' which is more precise than the general 'to praise.' A footnote could also note that the Hebrew here reads 'tribes of Yah,' a shortened form of the divine name.

text: For there the thrones of judgment stand, the thrones of the house of David.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: "May those who love you be at rest.

versions.text: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: "May those who love you prosper.
versions.explanation: The verb יִשְׁלָיוּ (from שׁלה) denotes being at ease, secure, or tranquil rather than material prosperity. It also echoes the words שָׁלוֹם and שַׁלְוָה in the surrounding verses, a sound-play that 'be at rest' preserves better for oral reading.

text: May there be peace within your walls, security within your palaces."
For the sake of my brothers and my friends, I will say, "Peace be within you."

versions.text: For the sake of my brothers and my friends, I will say, "Peace be with you."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew בָּךְ is 'within you' (addressed to the city), matching 'within your walls' in verse 7. 'With you' loses the spatial sense of peace dwelling inside Jerusalem.

text: For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good.
